Wide-tracked title caps set as an expanded geometric sans that sits around the eye's pupil, so the type is integrated with the image; credits are small, tracked and placed with restraint
Implied choreography: a match-cut logic from geology to biology to astrophysics to the eye, building to the title
gaps: The nebula-as-eye reveal draws on familiar NASA imagery, so the final beat is iconic rather than surprising
The credit typography is conventional; a more individual face would raise it further
The middle disc frame is busier and less resolved than the crater and shell shots

defects: The source credit in the top right ('September monthly mean extent') sits on the growing ice-edge rings, and the ring lines cut through the word 'monthly' in every frame from 1992 on.
The '1979 edge' label sits on the outer rings with no knockout or offset, so it gets harder to read as the rings stack up.
The two-line subtitle disappears abruptly between 2006 and 2014 instead of handing off to anything.
The year counter changes in place with no transition: the number just swaps while the layout stays fixed, so the biggest text on screen has no motion behaviour.
The bar chart grows one bar at a time at a steady rate, with no easing or emphasis until the red bar for 2012 appears.
The ice mass shrinks by uniform interpolation from year to year, with no overshoot, settle or texture change. In the 1/6 s pairs the edge just steps inward.
In the spectrogram, the build before the reveal (about 21–24 s) is a flat-topped broadband noise block that cuts off hard near 20 kHz. It reads as stock white noise, not designed sound.
The final red 'ice lost' fill is a flat tint over the rings. It has no light or depth, so it doesn't match the textured ice and grain elsewhere.
gaps: Motion: one locked 30 s frame where the only moving things are a counter, rings and bars, so roughly half the seconds look like the previous one. There's no camera move, change of scale or reframing to mark the decades or the 2012 record. Top studios would push in on 2012, pull out for the −36% reveal, and give the ring deposits some weight and settle so each year lands as an event rather than a step in an interpolation.

Sound: a mostly steady harmonic piano or mallet arpeggio with gentle phrase gaps, then a generic noise riser. There's no clear per-year tick tied to the rings, no low-end impact on the −36% reveal, and little texture beyond the main instrument. The dynamics read as a bed with one swell, not a mix scored to the data.

Finish and type: elegant restraint (a serif and mono pairing, a navy and ice palette with a red accent), but the type is static and doesn't carry the data. The year number doesn't change in weight, tracking or colour as the ice is lost, the labels collide with the rings, and the final red fill is flat next to the grain and cloud texture on the ice.
